data.note: Reflection: I called DNA replication (p=0.68) but the compound is lactacystin, annotated Protein degradation. Lactacystin is a 20S proteasome inhibitor (e.g. PMID 39988264 describes "20S proteasome inhibitor lactacystin"; PMID 27802243 reviews the proteasome-inhibition model). I over-weighted the high-dose atlas match to methotrexate/floxuridine and the dose-dependent cell enlargement with DNA loss, which mimics antimetabolite profiles, and under-weighted the microscopist warning of preserved microtubules/actin without polyploid or mitotic signature, plus the non-reproducible 0.3 uM DNA-high signal on replicate. What misled me was over-weighting the atlas comparison and high-dose morphology: e7 and e12 majorities for DNA replication over kinase inhibitors drowned out the single e11 hit that included Protein degradation 1/10, and I read the dose-dependent DNA loss (e8 rho=-1.00) as primary antimetabolite-like S-phase block. ## Conclusion

**DNA replication** (stated probability 0.68); key evidence e2, e7, e12, e13, e14, e6.

Why: Dose-dependent enlargement with DNA loss and atlas match to antimetabolites favors DNA replication.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Pulse EdU incorporation plus DNA-content flow cytometry and gamma-H2AX staining vs DMSO to test S-phase inhibition versus DNA breakage.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

The dose-dependent cell enlargement (cell_area rho=+0.99, e13) with DNA loss and cell-count reduction across independent high-dose wells (e2,e4,e5,e13,e14), combined high-dose atlas DNA replication 5/10 with top similarities over kinase 4/10 (e12), and non-specific but microtubule/actin-excluding phenotype (e6) favour DNA replication over kinase/DNA-damage runners-up. The failed 0.3uM DNA-high replication (e10 vs e3) weakens only the biphasic claim, not the replicated high-dose trend; 0.68 is reasonably calibrated.

## Unblinding

Compound: **lactacystin** (PubChem CID [6610292](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6610292))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **DNA replication**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

I predicted DNA replication (p=0.68) because high doses showed extreme cytoplasmic enlargement with DNA loss (e2 cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+9.3, nuc_dna_mean z=-8.4), dose-dependent cell_area increase (e13 rho=+0.99) and cell-count loss (e14 rho=-0.90), and atlas matches favoring DNA replication 5-6/10 in e7/e12. Truth was protein degradation for lactacystin, a 20S proteasome inhibitor (PMID 39988264).

What misled me was over-weighting the atlas comparison and high-dose morphology: e7 and e12 majorities for DNA replication over kinase inhibitors drowned out the single e11 hit that included Protein degradation 1/10, and I read the dose-dependent DNA loss (e8 rho=-1.00) as primary antimetabolite-like S-phase block. My acquisition plan focused on 1, 3 and 10 uM maximal toxicity (e2, e4, e5) plus a failed replication of the mid-dose DNA-high effect (e3 vs e10), and the non-specific microscopist call in e6 only excluded actin/microtubule, so no proteasome-discriminative measurement was ever made.

What was right was that the enlargement/cell-loss trends were real and the biphasic DNA claim was correctly weakened by e10, and protein degradation was retained at low probability. I missed that proteasome dysfunction secondarily alters cell-cycle, gene expression and protein turnover (PMID 16905641, PMID 15966900, PMID 30865843), which can mimic DNA-replication phenotypes at toxic high doses.

What was right:
- Quantified real dose-dependent cytoplasmic enlargement (e13 cell_area rho=+0.99) and cell loss (e14 cell_count rho=-0.90) across replicated high-dose wells e2, e4, e5.
- Correctly flagged non-reproducibility of the mid-dose DNA-high signal (e3 nuc_dna_mean z=+5.4 vs e10 showing only nuclear shape change).
- Retained protein degradation/DNA damage/kinase alternatives and used e6 to exclude actin/microtubule phenotypes.

What was wrong or missed:
- Assigned DNA replication 0.68 on atlas majorities e7/e12 (5-6/10) while discounting the e11 Protein degradation 1/10 signal that pointed to truth.
- Interpreted high-dose DNA loss (e2 nuc_dna_mean z=-8.4, e8 rho=-1.00) as direct S-phase inhibition rather than secondary cell-cycle/death effect of proteasome inhibition.
- Acquisition focused on high-dose toxicity mapping and atlas similarity without a proteasome-specific readout or proteasome-inhibitor reference comparison.

Proposed next experiment: Dose lactacystin alongside a proteasome-inhibitor control (e.g. bortezomib/MG132) and a DNA-replication control, then measure proteasome activity plus ubiquitin-conjugate accumulation by Western blot in parallel with EdU incorporation and DNA-content flow to test primary proteasome blockade versus direct S-phase inhibition.
